properties.description: Eight probes across engine and tool. ENGINE (tests/evidence_has_somewhere_to_go.rs): the constructor can reach `description` at all — the half that would otherwise have been missed, since the field was declared and unwritable; a run records `findings` beside its outcome; omitting `findings` LEAVES IT ALONE while a supplied `last_run_at` still moves; a later run can replace it, so "leaves alone" is distinguishable from "cannot update"; and name/description/findings survive independently, since conflating any two is the state the requirement exists to end. TOOL (tests/the_rollup_stays_cheap_to_read.rs): a 120-word name is shortened in loop_status AND carries name_truncated plus name_words plus a top-level note; a short name is untouched and claims no truncation — the counterweight without which the code could truncate everything and still pass; and description and findings are reachable through the MCP tools end to end.
properties.findings: 8/8 passing. Workspace 1287 tests, 0 failures. Written the new way as its own first demonstration: this check's name is 9 words against a corpus median of 76, its account is in `description`, and this sentence is in `findings` — the three fields the requirement asked to be separable, used separately.
properties.name: A check records what it found separately from what it is
